description:
## Question

The cosine top-k workload needs `[f32]` and PCM mixing needs `[i16]`/`[i32]` (see "Choose the target workload set"). Elixir has no f32 and no fixed-width integers, so these are divergence questions: when a kernel reads an element, what type does it get (f32 promoted to f64? i16 widened to i64?), what happens on a write that doesn't fit (raise, saturate, wrap: PCM clipping is saturation), is f32 arithmetic ever done in f32, and how does an Elixir caller build and read these arrays? The answer must fit the one rule.

comments.text: Per 'What is the one rule a kernel author keeps in their head?' (defk-dtw.7): [T] is a binary of native-endian T; reads follow the bitstring match (f32 widens to f64 with Elixir's rounding, narrow ints widen to i64); a write that doesn't fit its type raises (a limit; Elixir would wrap or store inf). PCM clipping is an explicit min/max.
Note from 'Should kernels offer opt-in wrapping integer arithmetic for hashes?' (defk-dtw.10): u64 and [u64] are decided there; this ticket covers [f32], [i16], [i32] (and any other narrow types).

Resolution (builds on the one rule's array decision in defk-dtw.7):
- Types added: [i16], [i32], [f32] only (demand-driven: PCM mixing, cosine top-k), beside [u8], [i64], [f64] and the decided [u64]. Other widths (i8, u16, u32) go under 'Where defk could grow'; the unknown-type compile error lists the supported set.
- Element types only: no narrow scalars. Reads widen as Elixir's bitstring match (i16/i32 -> i64, f32 -> f64 exactly).
- f32 writes round to nearest as <<v::float-32-native>> does; a value that rounds to +-inf raises (a limit: Elixir stores inf). Underflow to 0.0 and subnormals follow Elixir silently (same result; neither limit nor divergence). Integer writes out of range raise (as decided).
- Arithmetic is never done in f32; all float arithmetic is f64. The cosine top-k row records the cost against the NIF.
- inf/NaN bit patterns in input arrays ([f32] and existing [f64]): Elixir mode's match fails, so the kernel must raise; handed to 'Decide policy for inf/NaN inside kernels' (defk-q1c).
- Native endianness (matches existing types, Elixir mode, Nx binaries); one line in docs/language.md.
- Callers use plain binaries and documented bitstring forms or Nx; no helper module. A binary whose size isn't a multiple of the element width raises ArgumentError at the call.
- PCM clipping max(min(v, 32767), -32768) into [i16] must compile with no write check via the existing min/max range facts; a done criterion for the build.
Checked on OTP 29: <<0.1::float-32>> rounds; <<1.0e40::float-32>> and just-above-fmax store +inf; 1.0e-50 stores 0.0; 1.0e-40 keeps a subnormal; matching inf/NaN bits as float-32 fails.
Build handed off as [Add [i16], [i32] and [f32] element types](defk-4ai). Glossary: 'Element type' added to CONTEXT.md.

title: What do narrow element types ([f32], [i16], [i32]) mean in a kernel?
